candidates.name: negative_probe_margin_admits_trial
candidates.change: config.json: change "fit": {"probe_margin": 0.0, ...} to "probe_margin": -0.15. Nothing else changes.
candidates.hypothesis: The probe gate is the binding constraint, not the fitter: probe_margin is 0.0 and only 16/45 (binpack) and 16/44 (tsp) features ever reach a trial, while 24 are rejected by the probe every generation. With probe sigma 0.3, a margin of 0.0 accepts anything at noise level, so the gate is both too permissive to noise and (through the single-gain probe) too strict in practice. Lowering the margin lets near-neutral features be judged by the 16-eval trial instead of a one-shot probe, which is where the deep loop's kept features actually come from.

candidates.name: shift_one_mutator_slot_to_researcher
candidates.change: config.json: set "researcher": {"experiments": 5, ...} and "mutator": {"slots": 3, ...}; leave "mutator"."fresh": 1 unchanged (hooks.py computes fresh slots as slots - len(vary), so with 3 slots and 1 fresh the Mutator still gets two varied parents once the ledger has entries).
candidates.hypothesis: In generation 1 the Mutator has no parents (vary is empty in every digest: 'fresh 4'), so its slots produce blind variations that are mostly duplicates, while the kept features come from the deep loop (binpack: 3 kept deep, 0 wide). The budget is dominated by a loop that cannot use its slots in the generation where nearly all the gain happens (90% of final by gen 1-2). Moving one slot to the Researcher buys a fifth deep experiment per generation at the cost of a blind fresh slot.

--- prompts/mutator.md
-- **Fresh:** something that nothing on the scoreboard already does.
+- **Fresh:** something that nothing on the scoreboard already does. Reach for a quantity or a comparison the scoreboard hasn't touched at all, not a re-skin of what it already measures.
+
+Work in this order:
+1. Read the scoreboard for **shape**, not for a winner: which families of ideas exist, which are over-represented. Then deliberately go to an under-represented one, or outside all of them.
+2. When varying a parent, change the *form* (a comparison instead of a level, a ratio instead of a difference, a condition that switches it off for part of the candidates), not a constant.
+3. A near-miss (small positive gain, not kept) is a good parent: change the one thing that most likely stopped it from gaining more.
+4. Never mirror the parent's sign or its monotone shape: a sign flip or monotone transform is a duplicate.
+
+The **scoreboard** shows what was already evaluated and what happened to it (gain = how much better the result got; negative = worse). Don't reproduce any of it: disguised copies are detected and discarded without being evaluated.
--- prompts/navigator.md

-3. **Don't repeat the ledger.** If an idea was tried, change it meaningfully or leave it. A disguised copy is detected and discarded. When the ledger shows a group of tried features that behave alike, that idea is spent: look at a different quantity altogether.

nodes.title: probe gating and rejection
nodes.description: Change how cheap probes decide whether a feature is worth deep investment, so probe_rejected (8-25/run) stops discarding features that would have gained.

nodes.title: duplicate suppression
nodes.description: Reduce the 6-25 duplicates per run by making the Mutator see what was already tried and steering it away from near-identical features.

nodes.title: wide-loop breadth vs depth
nodes.description: Rebalance Mutator slot allocation and parent selection so wide variants explore genuinely different mechanisms instead of clustering.

nodes.title: early-generation targeting
nodes.description: Since 90% of gains land by gen 1-2, front-load effort: more experiments and better parent seeding in generation 0-1, less later.

nodes.title: researcher experiment design
nodes.description: Make the Researcher design sharper, falsifiable experiments (isolate one mechanism, predict direction) rather than broad feature edits.
